title: KYE Proposed Action
description: A candidate action submitted to KYE Admission Gate™ for admissibility check before any authority decisioning is performed. Carries origin, intent refs, requested capability, target resource, preconditions and risk flags.

action_declaration.description: Structured declaration of WHAT this action does — its execution-meaning and safety properties. A required INPUT to the Admission Gate for any action that affects system or physical state (robotics, IoT, vehicles, medical devices, industrial control): authorised does not imply safe. The action must be declared clearly enough for admissibility to evaluate. KYE checks the declaration is present and adequate; it does NOT compute the physical safety envelope itself (that is the declarer's / a functional-safety stack's responsibility, e.g. IEC 61508 / ISO 13849 / ISO 26262). See dictionary term action_declaration.

action_type.description: Canonical action verb being executed (e.g. open_valve, adjust_dosage, reroute_vehicle, transfer_funds, delete_record).

target_system_class.description: Class of system/state the action affects (e.g. database, payment_rail, robotic_arm, infusion_pump, vehicle_controller).

side_effects_declared.description: Declared side effects of executing the action. An empty array asserts 'no side effects'; absence of the field asserts 'undeclared'.

rollback_available.description: Whether a rollback / compensating action exists and is invocable.

stop_condition_present.description: Whether an emergency-stop / abort path is defined for the action.

safe_state_precondition.description: The system/physical state that must hold for the action to be safe to execute (evaluated by the declarer's safety controller, not by KYE).

action_risk_classification.description: The explicit Action Risk Classification step that runs AFTER Action Declaration and BEFORE Action Admissibility (pipeline: Intent -> Action Declaration -> Action Risk Classification -> Action Admissibility -> Authority Resolution -> ...). It classifies the proposed action's risk so admissibility can apply DYNAMIC AUTHORITY GATES: a low-risk action takes the light path; a high/unacceptable-risk action demands deeper evidence and a stronger oversight mode. KYE does not invent a parallel risk model — it REUSES the canonical risk_tier vocabulary (kye.risk_assessment.v1) and the signed score (kye.risk.score.v1). See dictionary term action_risk_classification.

risk_tier.description: Canonical risk tier — REUSED from kye.risk_assessment.v1 (EU AI Act-aligned), never redefined. 'prohibited'/'unacceptable' short-circuit to reject; 'high' escalates the required oversight mode.

risk_score_ref.description: Pointer to the signed kye.risk.score.v1 record this classification is based on (score + risk_class + signals), so the classification is evidenced, not asserted.

classification_basis.description: The signals/risk_flags that drove the tier (e.g. effect_class=safety_critical, prohibited_category_detected, irreversible-no-rollback).

required_oversight_mode.description: The §36 GovernedUI oversight mode the tier maps to — the Dynamic Authority Gate. Higher risk -> stronger mode. REUSED from the §36 approval-mode enum, never redefined.
